Hi Samantha / Procurement team,

Great talking yesterday — glad to see Crestview moving to expand usage. Attached is our consolidated renewal package (Crestview_Renewal_Draft_v3.docx) and an updated order form (OrderForm_v2.xlsx) reflecting the +30% token uplift and proposed 18-month term.

Two quick asks so we can keep the cadence:
- Can your legal send any MSA redlines back by EOD Friday (we saw a few notes verbally but want them in one file)?
- Any procurement-specific PO identifiers we should include on the order form?

We’ve flagged the key negotiation items in the draft: term length (12 vs 18 months), SLA credits for sustained latency, and a minor data residency carve-out for a regulated subset. If your team prefers, I can send a consolidated redline response once we have their initial pass.

Proposed timeline: redlines in by 5/14 -> Redwood response by 5/17 -> go-to-sign on 5/19 (DocuSign link to follow). Is that workable?

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that helps speed things up.

Best,
David

Thanks David — this looks promising. A few clarifications from our side before legal redlines: 

- Term: we prefer 18 months if the price tier for months 13–18 is not higher than months 1–12. Can you confirm planned unit pricing in the order form for the full 18 months?
- Capacity: the +30% uplift is fine but we need a clear overage policy (how bursting is billed).
- Data residency: we’ll route the regulated subset through our EU tenant — need to confirm that’s acceptable for the limited set of datasets.

Looping in ProcureOps for PO and legal. They’ll send MSA redlines as a tracked document by 5/14 if all good.

—Samantha
